title: AI Native by Design: Lessons Learned from Building NVIDIA TensorRT Model Connect | NVIDIA Technical Blog
text:
Parallel work, model family isolation, reversible changes, and GPU-backed validation shaped an open source project designed around coding agents
By Yifei Fang
NVIDIA TensorRT Model Connect is an open source collection of AI model reference implementations in C++ built on NVIDIA TensorRT.
The project demonstrates AI-native development by treating AI outputs as modular, verifiable units of work isolated to prevent error cascades.
Engineering choices include selecting horizontally scalable work, providing agents with outcomes and references instead of recipes, and isolating model-family changes so failures remain local.
Validation relies on human-legible evidence, agent-native self-improving tests, reproducible CI, and adversarial collaboration between QA and developers.
Human judgment shifts upstream to designing the system, setting acceptance criteria, and remaining accountable for release decisions.
Follow the Quick Start to build and run a supported model.
Explore Supported Models and their qualification evidence.
Read the AI and Agent Guide .
Parallel work, model-family isolation, reversible changes, and GPU-backed validation shaped an open source project designed around coding agents
NVIDIA TensorRT Model Connect is an open source collection of AI model reference implementations in C++, built on top of NVIDIA TensorRT . It began with a practical question: could the performance of the NVIDIA inference stack be made accessible to model developers who are not TensorRT experts?
The NVIDIA team initially approached the project as an experiment with coding agents. Within the first few days, however, the interest shifted to a larger question: what would it mean to design a serious software project around AI agents from the beginning—not merely use an agent to accelerate an existing development process?
The answer has not been an elaborate orchestration system or an ever-growing collection of prompts. It has been a set of engineering choices:
AI increases the rate at which candidate implementations can be produced. Architecture and validation determine whether that increased output becomes reliable software.
What does it mean to call TensorRT Model Connect AI native?
AI native can mean many things. In reference to TensorRT Model Connect, the term is used in a narrow, operational sense. AI-native projects treat AI outputs as modular, verifiable units of work. Isolating these units prevents errors from cascading, ensuring that the inherent unpredictability of AI models does not compromise system stability.
This does not mean that AI writes everything. It does not mean that human judgment disappears. And it does not mean that every software project should adopt the same model. Nor does it mean code emitted without supervision; rather, it refers to a production system capable of exploring many candidate changes and subjecting each one to repeatable quality control. Compute helps create the candidates. Tests, reference comparisons, benchmarks, and human review determine what is ready for shipping.
The following sections explain the lessons learned from building AI-native TensorRT Model Connect.
Start with work that can scale horizontally
Some engineering workloads have a long serial critical path. Others comprise many independent workstreams. Adding agents helps far more in the second category.
The long tail of AI models is a natural fit for horizontal work. Model families, configurations, operators, runtime paths, and validation cases can often be investigated independently. Work on one model family does not always need to block work on another.
The geometry of that problem is central to TensorRT Model Connect.
The project provides family-owned reference implementations that turn supported Hugging Face or local checkpoints into versioned .bundle artifacts, then expose task-oriented native C++ APIs for text, vision, audio, diffusion, segmentation, embedding, forecasting, and other workloads. The build and runtime boundary is documented in the TensorRT Model Connect Project Overview .
As of the public July 29, 2026 release comparison, the project covered 128 model families tested on NVIDIA GB300. That number is not, in itself, a measure of agent productivity. It does show why the problem benefits from an architecture that can grow by adding independent units rather than extending one serial integration path.
The first lesson is therefore simple: AI-native development begins with problem selection. If work cannot be decomposed into parallel tasks, adding more agents mostly introduces coordination overhead and the potential for error cascades.
Provide agents with outcomes and references, not recipes
Most TensorRT Model Connect agent runs begin with an outcome: support a model family, close an accuracy gap, improve a performance path, or strengthen a contract. The evidence required to accept the result is also identified. This often includes behavior from an established reference implementation, plus project-specific tests and constraints.
The process intentionally began with a simple outer loop: a high-level goal, a general-purpose coding agent, repository instructions, and strict validation. Humans currently continue to initiate most long-running tasks. Prescribing the full implementation plan is generally avoided unless the task or an observed failure mode requires it.
The working hypothesis is that a capable general-purpose agent benefits from room to use patterns it has already learned. Instead of encoding an engineer’s preferred implementation into every prompt, specify the result, the boundaries, and the evidence required.
The implementation path is flexible. The acceptance criteria are not.
This is minimal orchestration, not minimal control. The agent may explore, implement, test, fail, and revise inside an isolated task. The resulting change must still satisfy the same architectural and technical gates as any other contribution. Constraints are added when repeated evidence shows they are needed, not simply because a workflow can be hard-coded.
The most important constraint on AI-native development has not been the agent’s ability to complete an individual task. It has been the architecture surrounding that task.
For TensorRT Model Connect, components that evolve at different speeds were separated:
TensorRT and CUDA form the stable execution foundation: Compatibility, performance, reliability, and long-term contracts matter here.
TensorRT Model Connect is the faster-moving integration layer: It connects a broad and rapidly changing model ecosystem to that foundation.
Model-family implementations own model-specific knowledge: Builders, runtime pipelines, helper kernels, configuration, and validation evidence stay with the family that needs them.
This design prioritizes independence. While shared abstractions can reduce code volume, they often couple unrelated tasks, increase merge conflicts, and expand the impact of potential errors. Some redundancy between similar model families is an acceptable trade-off for scaling.
Therefore, promote behavior into shared infrastructure only when multiple independent owners need the same assumption-free contract. Everything else stays close to the model family that owns it. The public TensorRT Model Connect Units and Ownership documentation makes those boundaries explicit.
Isolation does not eliminate all systemic risk: shared build, runtime, packaging, and CI infrastructure can still affect multiple families. But it materially reduces the number of changes that must move together and makes parallel work safer.
Isolation is paired with reversibility. Two-way doors are preferred: make changes that are easy to evaluate, simple to revert, and unlikely to cascade into unrelated model families. This approach enables rapid learning without mistaking speed for permission to weaken the system.
When candidate code becomes cheaper, evidence becomes more expensive
AI makes candidate implementations cheap. It does not make correctness cheap. Only a small number of candidates survive automation and human judgment.
Make evidence human-legible: Machine checks are necessary, but a reviewer cannot quickly interpret a pile of tensors or raw values. Semantic task interfaces—text in/text out or text in/image out—make final behavior legible enough for a human to spot-check quickly. A spot check is not proof. It complements automated tests by ensuring that their evidence ends in behavior a person can understand.
Make validation agent-native and self-improving: Agents can generate tests, probes, and operating procedures alongside the code, then refine them as real artifacts expose missing assumptions. If automated checks pass but a human finds a bad final artifact, the process has admitted a false success.
Reproduce: Reproduce the failure, encode the missing invariant or regression, and harden the SOP so the next run is harder to fool.
Make QA and development adversarial collaborators: QA is not a downstream team that receives a finished implementation. QA and developers operate on the same reproducible CI pipeline from organizationally independent positions. QA should function much like a red team attempting to falsify the implementation’s claims. Developers harden the implementation and the pipeline in response. Shared evidence makes findings reproducible. Independent ownership keeps the challenge credible.
Candidate code can scale with agents and tokens. Trustworthy software can scale only as fast as its evidence and validation system.
The practical effect of this approach is that every engineer takes on work that resembles management and direction. The highest-leverage questions move upstream:
What problem is worth solving?
Can the work be decomposed and scaled safely?
What technical and organizational constraints can turn untrusted candidate outputs into a result that deserves trust?
Agent outputs begin as untrusted candidates. Model-family ownership, reversible changes, independent QA challenge, reproducible CI, and human-legible evidence do not guarantee correctness. They make claims falsifiable, failures easier to contain, and acceptance or rejection easier to review.
Humans still inspect implementations and debug failures. But their most valuable work increasingly lies in designing and governing the system: setting intent and acceptance criteria, deciding where independence is required, interpreting anomalous evidence, and remaining accountable for release.
What aspects of TensorRT Model Connect remain unsolved?
TensorRT Model Connect is currently in public preview, and several parts of this model are still being tested and refined.
Not every engineering task can be decomposed into independent units.
Minimal project-specific orchestration is not a universal best practice. Adding structure is expected where repeated failures justify it.
Model-family isolation reduces blast radius but cannot eliminate failures in shared infrastructure.
Reference implementations are useful comparison points, not infallible oracles. Tests also need independent invariants and carefully reviewed tolerances.
More parallel agents can increase demand for validation faster than they increase accepted throughput.
Most tasks are still initiated by humans. Automated task discovery and large-scale concurrency are future directions, not claims about the current system.
These limitations are not incidental. They define the engineering work required to make AI-native development dependable.
Moving from a production model to a better developer experience
The purpose of this work is not just the inference system itself. It is the developer experience that the system can make possible.
Model developers should not need to become inference experts before they can evaluate and deploy a supported model efficiently on NVIDIA hardware. TensorRT Model Connect aims to provide a clear path from a Hugging Face or local checkpoint to a versioned bundle and native task API, while keeping the model-family implementation visible enough to inspect, extend, and customize.
The longer-term aspiration is straightforward: connect a model through a stable boundary, then continue benefiting as TensorRT, CUDA, kernels, compilers, and supported NVIDIA platforms improve underneath it. Note that this is an aspirational goal rather than a guarantee of current compatibility for every model or target. For more detailed information, refer to the TensorRT-Model-Connect documentation .
TensorRT Model Connect will succeed only if it lowers the expertise barrier while preserving the accuracy, performance, reliability, and maintainability developers expect.
That is also the larger promise of AI-native development: not code for its own sake, but a means to make previously expensive, fragmented engineering problems economically possible—without giving up evidence, accountability, or quality.
Try TensorRT Model Connect and help improve it
TensorRT Model Connect is open source and evolving rapidly. Want to get involved?
The team is still learning what an AI-native open source project should look like. The most valuable feedback will come from developers who try it, inspect its evidence, find its limits, and help improve the boundaries.
Yifei Fang is a senior software engineer on the NVIDIA TensorRT team, where he leads the AI-Native Software initiative for NVIDIA TensorRT Model Connect. His work focuses on expanding model support across the TensorRT ecosystem and fostering a vibrant community around framework-independent inference software.

title: OPEC Expected to Keep Oil Production Quotas Unchanged
text:
By Charles Kennedy - Sep 30, 2026, 8:30 AM CDT
The key OPEC+ producers are set to leave their current crude oil output quotas unchanged for November at a meeting this weekend, anonymous sources familiar with the plans told Reuters on Wednesday.
The Gulf producers in OPEC+ have been producing and exporting much lower volumes sin ce the Iran war crippled traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
In the early September monthly meeting, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman decided to maintain the September 2026 required production quotas for October 2026, after having unwound a total of 1.65 million barrels per day (bpd) of collective cuts that began in 2023.
OPEC+ has been raising nominal production quotas for most of this year, but actual supply to the market has been well below the required levels of production, due to the Middle East conflict.
Crude oil production at many of the Gulf states has been seriously lagging behind the OPEC+ quotas, which have more or less become irrelevant since March as the Strait of Hormuz disruptions trapped a significant part of supply in the Persian Gulf.
The producer group, led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, appears to have shifted its focus to debates and discussions about the 2027 quotas, which the alliance plans to review and set the baselines for any cuts going forward.
In recent weeks, OPEC’s oil production fell in August due to lower Saudi supply, but the output at the core OPEC+ producers increased.
Saudi Arabia’s oil production fell in August amid Houthi threats to shipments in the Red Sea, dragging OPEC’s output down, a Bloomberg survey showed .
But OPEC’s data in its Monthly Oil Market Report (MOMR) for September showed that total crude oil production in the whole OPEC+ alliance averaged 38.05 million bpd in August 2026, up by 300,000 bpd higher compared to July.
Production at OPEC+ is about 5 million bpd lower compared to pre-war levels, as almost all OPEC Gulf members are trailing behind their quotas due to the ongoing shipping disruptions.
By Charles Kennedy for Oilprice.com

title: Nvidia raises the Shield TV Pro price by $100—seven years after launch - How-To Geek
text:
By Jon Fingas
Nvidia might have released the Shield TV Pro in 2019, but even that device isn't immune to market pressure. The company has raised the price of the Shield TV Pro to $300, a $100 hike.
The company explains the move to 9to5 Google as the result of the technology cost crisis prompted by the AI data center rush. "The cost of components, including memory, has increased substantially across the industry," Nvidia says in a statement.
Nvidia has simultaneously discontinued the standard Shield TV. The Android TV hardware has been sold out for months, but it's now clear no new stock is coming. The firm hasn't said if there will be any future Shield products.
Not every store is reflecting the Shield TV Pro price increase, so you'll want to buy quickly if you're interested.
Other brands have already increased their prices. The Apple TV 4K jumped from $129 to $199, while the Google TV Streamer surged from $100 to $150. Even Roku's typically affordable streaming devices are more expensive, starting at $40 (previously $30) for the Streaming Stick .
Is the Shield TV Pro still a good deal?
The Shield TV Pro is old, but its powerful-for-the-time Tegra X1+ chip has kept it relevant for years. It can play 4K HDR video, upscale lower-resolution content, and play games either from the Google Play Store or through the cloud using GeForce Now . It can double as a Plex media server .
By Tim Brookes
The higher price nonetheless hurts its value. You're now paying $300 for the media streamer when newer boxes cost much less, and might be better for gaming and other more demanding tasks. And while Nvidia is still updating the software to this day, it's capped at Android 11 where the latest Android TV software is based on Android 16. That leaves it without underlying features and potentially exposes it to security risks.
There are few options for dedicated Android TV devices, however, and they tend to be less powerful products like the Google TV Streamer and Walmart's Onn 4K Pro . If you prefer Google's take on the living room and don't have a TV set with Android built-in, the Shield TV Pro is still a good choice.
So Nvidia is one of the reasons prices have gone up and had made buckets of money, yet $hits on it consumers with outdated tech? 😆 I have owned multiple shields and this is outrageous.
The 2019 Shield Pro is not worth $300. Did the price increase on current stock in stores? When were they manufactured? This seems like the dumbest move given the hardware hasn't been updated since 2019. I'm glad bought my 2 devices years ago.
Even with the 2019 hardware refresh the Shield TV is using obsolete, outdated hardware from well over a decade ago. The OG Shield TV CPU was already obsolete before the Shield TV even launched. Why? The Tegra X1/X1+ only has 4 big CPU cores that work, while every other ARM chipset had 4 big & 4 LITTLE cores. This means the OG Shield TV was falsely advertised as being something it wasn't.
Shield is still the best but I agree its not worth $300. I also have two and one is still sealed. Also grabbed a couple google streamers for $70 each when on sale. Have a couple chromecast 4k still sealed as well I bought on sale for $30. I guess hoarding sale items sometimes pays off.
JM It is absolutely obsolete. It doesn't do anything people need today. Nvidia cancelled it, so any existing units are obsolete by definition. It is the Nvidia Shield TV Pro that got the price hike. The commenter was referring to the discontinued model, not the one that can act as a dedicated plex server and other things better than modern units. THAT one is not obsolete.
Christopher She Shield TV is so amazing that Nvidia cancelled it? He was referring to the Shield TV (obsolete and cancelled) NOT the Shield TV Pro ( still relevant and got a price hike).
Nvidia has no issues with increasing the price on something that’s almost a decade old. But they don’t want to make an updated version of the Shield, smh.
I have 1 of each of the Shields, not using any of them at the moment. They all work, though the Shield Tablet is a bit slow compared to other tablets I own. It was nice when it was new. Not sure if I ever will use the Shield Pro again. If they produce a Shield Pro 2 I'd buy it.

title: Greg Lui Arrested Over Alleged $300 Million Nvidia Server Smuggling to China
text:
Greg Lui Arrested Over Alleged $300 Million Nvidia Server Smuggling to China
Greg Lui of Earthmade is accused of shipping over $300 million in Nvidia servers to China through Malaysia and Singapore, federal prosecutors say.
Greg Lui, 38, owner of California-based Earthmade Computer, was arrested on October 1, 2026 on charges of sending servers with Nvidia chips worth more than $300 million to China, sidestepping U.S. export licenses through two stopovers in Malaysia and Singapore. The Department of Justice (DOJ) disclosed the case in a press release, but it remains an allegation and Lui is presumed innocent until a verdict.
The grand jury indictment (the panel that decides whether a case goes to trial), filed on September 29 at the federal court in Los Angeles, yields flight dates, order numbers and airline names. Such details are rare in a case like this, and they let readers follow the servers step by step.
Beijing has since announced export controls on 23 AI technologies, with models and agents in scope .
On October 10, two leakers then claimed that Nvidia is ending the RTX 5090 and reserving GB202 chips for RTX PRO , with no official confirmation.
The case file (case 2:26-cr-00618, Central District of California) contains three counts. The first is conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act, the U.S. law on sensitive exports, together with the Export Administration Regulations (EAR), the implementing rules of the Commerce Department. The second is smuggling out of the country, meaning help in getting goods to leave in violation of those rules. The third is conspiracy to commit money laundering.
The maximum penalty is 20 years on the first count and 10 on the second, with another 20 on the third. The 50-year sum that appears in some outlets is a theoretical ceiling, because it ignores how a judge combines sentences, while Tom's Hardware headlines "up to 20 years" by looking at a single count.
The FBI investigated alongside the Export Enforcement office of the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS, the Commerce agency that polices dual-use technology) and the Pentagon's Defense Criminal Investigative Service. "SI is the defining technology of the era," John A. Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for national security, said in the release, where "SI" stands for artificial superintelligence in DOJ parlance.
Earthmade was incorporated on November 10, 2023 in City of Industry, near Los Angeles. Lui served as its chief executive. According to the prosecution, the company ordered servers with Nvidia GPUs from three U.S. manufacturers (the indictment does not name them) and stated that the end buyers were in countries where no license is needed. Those countries were Malaysia and Singapore. From there the machines allegedly continued to China.
The money, again in the prosecutors' account, came from two Malaysian companies. Between January and October 2024 Earthmade allegedly collected more than $80 million from the first and $96 million from the second, or $176 million in total. The first, founded in 1999, dealt in timber, plywood and panels (a curious stop for artificial intelligence hardware). The second is described as a front company. The ultimate recipient would be an industrial group in Hangzhou, never named.
The indictment cites four episodes.
On January 30, 2024, Lui orders 27 servers with H100 GPUs for about $7.6 million ($7,614,000). They leave Los Angeles for Kuala Lumpur the next day, and on March 12 an unindicted co-conspirator writes to a Malaysian government official that the machines were passed on to the Chinese buyer.
On June 15, 92 servers from a larger order (512 machines quoted on April 30) leave San Francisco airport on Singapore Airlines flight SQ0033 to Kuala Lumpur, then on Cathay Pacific CX722 to Hong Kong. The Chinese company appears as the consignee.
On July 2, an order of 100 servers with H100 chips, worth more than $22 million, goes out through a U.S. company used as a shield. The buyer is listed as Topmost, with a director named Jackie Lui who appears in documents alleged to be false.
The indictment adds that in 2021 Lui allegedly bought a person's identity documents and used that identity for transactions in the scheme.
Allegations only. The defendant is presumed innocent.
Source: DOJ indictment (case 2:26-cr-00618). Allegations only, the defendant is presumed innocent.
Which chips are involved and why a license is required
The indictment names Nvidia A100 and H100 GPUs (data center accelerators) and PNY GeForce RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 cards, all under the entry ECCN 4A090.a of the Commerce control list, which requires a license for exports to China. Under the EAR, Hong Kong counts the same as mainland China. The BIS introduced controls on advanced chips on October 7, 2022 and extended them with two rules dated October 25, 2023, in force from November 17. According to the indictment, neither Lui nor Earthmade ever applied for a license, for any destination.
The alleged mechanism is straightforward. No license was required for Malaysia and Singapore, so declaring them as final destinations was enough. The re-export to China, which does require one, allegedly happened afterward, with export filings (the EEIs, the electronic declarations that accompany every shipment) filled out with false classification codes to hide the nature of the goods.
The three U.S. manufacturers appear only as "US Manufacturer 1, 2 and 3." The indictment calls a sales manager at the first manufacturer, who allegedly approved the sale to Earthmade, Unindicted Co-Conspirator 1. Unindicted Co-Conspirator 5 is an executive at a U.S. freight forwarder. "Unindicted" simply means that the person is not named among the defendants in this indictment.
Nvidia is not a party to the case, and the sources consulted contain no comment from the company. The chips carry its brand, but the servers were designed and assembled by other U.S. companies.
The numbers in the indictment do not fully line up either. The introduction speaks of "more than $300 million" and paragraph 36 of "nearly three hundred million" in servers brokered, while the scheme period runs from "no later than October 2023" to "at least August 12, 2026" in the counts, after an opening that says "beginning in 2024." The DOJ release refers to 2023 and 2024. The differences do not change the structure of the case, but it pays to cite the exact paragraph when reporting figures.
The case does not come out of nowhere. In November 2025 the DOJ had indicted four people over a smaller operation, $3.89 million in wire transfers from China and A100 GPUs routed through Malaysia and Thailand, as The Register reported at the time . Beijing, for its part, had already called Anthropic's proposed AI slowdown a Cold War tactic in mid-September. The standoff between Washington and Beijing over sensitive technology runs through there as well.
Meanwhile China builds the alternative at home, from Huawei's Atlas 960E supercomputer to Alibaba's Zhenwu V900 chip . DeepSeek and Huawei are also working on TileLang to bring software to Ascend chips. Cases like this one show, however, that Nvidia chips remain in high demand. It is not the only story of controls sidestepped through unexpected middlemen, as the trick of Chinese sex toys used for Russian military electronics shows.
1. Is Nvidia accused of anything?
Short answer. Nvidia is not accused of anything in this indictment. The document names it only as the maker of the GPUs installed in the servers, while sales to Earthmade run through three unidentified U.S. companies.
2. Why Malaysia and Singapore?
Short answer. According to the prosecution, Malaysia and Singapore were chosen because buying those servers there requires no U.S. license. The indictment describes countries that did not impose one, used as a stopover before re-export to China, where a license is required. Of the two Malaysian companies that allegedly served as the bridge, the first began as a timber business and the second is described as a front company.
3. How much time does Greg Lui face?
Short answer. On paper, Greg Lui faces up to 20 years on each of the two conspiracy counts and up to 10 for smuggling, but those are statutory ceilings rather than a predicted sentence. The indictment also seeks forfeiture of the proceeds, while the sources consulted give no trial date yet.
4. Are the RTX 4090 and 5090 AI servers?
Short answer. No, the RTX 4090 and 5090 are consumer graphics cards. The indictment lists them under the same 4A090.a classification as the data center GPUs, but the smuggling count specifically targets servers with A100 and H100 chips.
Three things are still missing, namely a trial date, the names of the U.S. manufacturers and a word from Nvidia. Until they arrive, the indictment remains what it is, the prosecution's account with more detail than usual, built from orders, flights and front companies.
Flight SQ0033, a plywood supplier and a manager who allegedly approved the sales make a story worth following until the first hearing on the merits.

title: Trump adviser Hassett calls on Powell to leave Fed board after renovation report
text:
White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett called on former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to leave the central bank’s board following an internal watchdog report that criticized management of the Fed’s $2.4 billion headquarters renovation.
“I think that it’s time for him to move on and to respect the independence of the Fed,” Hassett, director of the National Economic Council, said Sunday on Fox News.
The Fed inspector general said in a Sept. 30 report that it found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing or administrative misconduct related to the renovation. However, the watchdog identified management shortcomings that contributed to the project's cost nearly doubling from its original estimate.
President Donald Trump responded by saying Powell “should be forced to resign from the Board.” Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday that the Justice Department wouldn't reopen a criminal investigation based on the inspector general's findings, although prosecutors could act if a separate audit uncovers evidence of criminal conduct.
The renewed pressure on Powell adds another political dimension to concerns about Federal Reserve independence, an issue closely watched by bond, currency and equity markets. Powell remains a Fed governor even though Kevin Warsh succeeded him as chair in May, meaning Powell continues to have a vote on monetary policy as the central bank confronts persistent inflation and rising borrowing costs.
Powell's continued presence is unusual because former Fed chairs typically leave the central bank's board after giving up the leadership role. Powell has said threats of investigations into him and the Fed contributed to his decision to remain.
The dispute comes after the Fed unanimously raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter percentage point last month. Hassett said he opposed the increase but defended the central bank's ability to make the decision independently. “As you saw, that Chairman Warsh voted with people to increase interest rates,” Hassett said. “I disagree with that decision, but we respect that he was doing that for the right reasons.”
Trump has said Warsh should make his own monetary-policy decisions, although he told Time magazine of the latest rate increase: “I probably would have voted against the board if I were him.”

title: SpaceX Wants to Borrow $40 Billion to Buy Nvidia Chips
text:
SpaceX is borrowing $40 billion for NVIDIA chips while posting a $541 million quarterly loss on capex more than double its revenue.
Apollo Global Management is expected to lead the deal, as Morgan Stanley warns AI infrastructure will need $1.5 trillion in outside financing by 2028.
Lockup expirations will release up to 1.3 billion SpaceX shares after Q3 earnings, pressuring stock as insiders sell right after a post-IPO rally.
A recent report citing people familiar with the matter said SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX ) is seeking about $40 billion of financing to pay for an order of AI chips from NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ). In after-hours trading, SpaceX fell about 1%, and NVIDIA rose about 0.5%.
Under the reported plan, SpaceX would take on the debt to fund the purchase, while NVIDIA would record the chip order as revenue when it ships.
SpaceX, Apollo Global Management ( NYSE:APO ) and NVIDIA did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The financing remains at the discussion stage.
What SpaceX Has Committed Versus What It Only Seeks
SpaceX is reportedly seeking about $10 billion in bank loans and about $30 billion in investment-grade debt. Investment-grade means bonds rated as having low default risk, which pension funds and insurance companies can hold.
The bank loans are the easier part, because a small group of lenders can agree on terms quickly, but selling bonds that large to a wide investor base requires work with rating agencies and a marketing process that takes quarters.
Apollo is expected to lead the deal and place pieces with other buyers. Pimco is among the lenders in talks.
The financing is expected to close in 2027, which means the terms, the lender group and the final size could all still change before any money moves.
In the second quarter of 2026, SpaceX reported revenue of $7.81 billion against capital spending of $18.37 billion, of which $15.83 billion went to AI. It posted a net loss of $541 million.
On the August 4 earnings call, management said the next two quarters should look "very similar" on spending, and Elon Musk said, "So we're exclusive to NVIDIA."
Borrowing avoids diluting shareholders today. Even so, lockup expirations will add 328.4 million marketable shares on October 9, another 328.4 million on October 24 and up to 1.3 billion after third-quarter earnings.
The stock priced at $135 in its June 11, 2026 initial public offering, peaked at $225.64 and closed at $171.92 on October 6. That close came one session after a 7.63% gain to its highest close since June, so insiders got their first chance to sell right after a rally, as the debt was being marketed.
NVIDIA closed at $239.24 after a record intraday high of $243.37, worth about $5.78 trillion. A large order matters, but at that size, no single customer changes the business.
Morgan Stanley ( NYSE:MS ) estimates AI infrastructure will need $1.5 trillion of outside financing by 2028. When more buyers borrow to pay for chips, NVIDIA's revenue stability depends in part on whether those buyers can carry their debt.
Analysts are bullish. Adam Jonas carries a $300 target, Eric Sheridan of Goldman Sachs ( NYSE:GS ) is at $230, and the average is near $235. Those targets assume the spending pays off, and lenders are now being asked to fund that same plan with debt.
At a market value of about $2.2 trillion to $2.3 trillion, with losses, heavy borrowing, and new share supply, SpaceX carries risks that the analyst targets may not fully reflect.
NVIDIA's exposure to the same AI spending carries less balance-sheet risk, because it gets paid when the chips ship, while SpaceX carries the debt for years. The power, cooling, and networking suppliers behind the expansion sit in a similar spot, paid up front as capacity gets built (we covered seven of them in a free report here).
It will be worth tracking whether SpaceX confirms the financing in a filing, whether rating agencies publicly engage, and whether the stock holds $171.92 through the October 24 unlock.

title: Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition Launches: What Nvidia RTX Spark Means for the Channel
text:
Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition brings Nvidia RTX Spark and up to 128GB memory. Explore its $3,799 starting price and what it means for channel partners.
Dell is bringing Nvidia’s RTX Spark technology to its XPS laptop lineup, offering up to 128GB of unified memory in a portable system designed for demanding AI and creative workloads.
The company revealed additional specifications, pricing, and preorder details for the XPS 16 Creator Edition on October 7. The laptop starts at $3,799.99 and combines an Nvidia Grace CPU with Blackwell RTX graphics, giving developers and creators another option for running supported AI models locally.
For businesses evaluating AI-capable hardware, the launch raises a practical question: Can powerful local AI processing justify spending nearly $4,000 on a laptop?
Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition: Key specifications and features
The XPS 16 Creator Edition is Dell’s first XPS laptop powered by Nvidia RTX Spark, a computing platform that combines CPU processing, GPU acceleration, and unified memory.
According to Dell’s product breakdown , the laptop supports configurations with up to 20 Nvidia Grace CPU cores and a Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores.
Unlike conventional laptops with separate system memory and dedicated graphics memory, RTX Spark uses a shared memory architecture. This allows supported AI and creative workloads to access a common memory pool.
Key specifications include:
Processor: Nvidia Grace CPU with up to 20 cores
Graphics: Nvidia Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 cores
Memory: Up to 128GB of unified memory
Display: 16-inch 3.2K Tandem OLED
Thickness: Approximately 0.7 inches (17.8mm)
Connectivity: HDMI 2.1b, three USB4 Type-C ports, full-size SDXC card reader, and audio jack
Operating system: Windows 11, with native Arm applications and support for compatible x86 applications through Prism emulation
According to Dell, the OLED display delivers up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness for HDR highlights and covers 100% of the DCI-P3 color gamut.
Unlike many mainstream AI PCs that emphasize a dedicated neural processing unit, RTX Spark combines an Arm-based Grace CPU, Blackwell RTX graphics, and shared memory to accelerate more demanding AI and creative workloads.
Dell also says the laptop natively supports creative applications, including Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Premiere, Blender, and DaVinci Resolve.
However, software compatibility remains an important consideration. Other applications, including MATLAB, rely on Windows’ Prism emulation layer. Compatibility and performance may vary depending on the software.
Nvidia RTX Spark brings local AI processing to Windows laptops
The XPS 16 Creator Edition is part of a broader effort by Dell, Nvidia, and Microsoft to make advanced AI processing available directly on Windows devices.
Dell says the laptop supports development tools including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, ComfyUI, and Cursor. Developers can also access Nvidia’s CUDA ecosystem and Linux AI frameworks via the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), enabling them to build and test supported AI workloads locally.
This could be useful for organizations experimenting with AI applications that require substantial computing resources but do not always need cloud-based processing.
Running supported AI models locally could reduce reliance on cloud infrastructure for certain workloads, although the financial benefits depend on hardware costs, utilization, and the applications involved.
Local processing also does not automatically eliminate security, privacy, or management concerns.
The launch comes as manufacturers expand their AI-capable PC lineups, offering specialized systems alongside conventional enterprise laptops.
Channel Insider previously examined how AI PCs are affecting enterprise hardware refresh decisions , particularly as organizations weigh the benefits of local processing against higher device costs.
The XPS 16 Creator Edition represents a more specialized version of that trend, targeting developers, creative professionals, and users who need considerably more processing power than a standard productivity laptop.
Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition pricing and US availability
Dell confirmed that the XPS 16 Creator Edition became available for US preorder through Best Buy on Oct. 7, with pricing starting at $3,799.99. Best Buy lists Oct. 16, 2026, as the laptop’s release date, although delivery estimates may vary by location and availability. Dell has not announced a separate general shipping date.
Although Dell says the laptop supports up to 128GB of unified memory, it has not published pricing for every available configuration. The company also says the laptop will be available on Dell.com, although it has not provided a specific date for that channel.
Buyers should check individual product listings to determine which processor, memory, and storage specifications are included at each price point.
The XPS 16 Creator Edition is also part of a broader Dell hardware announcement covering additional AI-focused systems.
The Dell Creator Edition Desktop uses the same Nvidia RTX Spark platform, while the Dell Pro Precision with GB300 workstation is gaining Windows support. Both are listed as coming soon, without specific availability dates.
What the new Dell laptop means for channel partners
For resellers, MSPs, and other channel partners, the XPS 16 Creator Edition introduces another premium hardware option for customers exploring local AI development.
Its high starting price means it is unlikely to replace conventional business laptops across entire organizations. Instead, the most immediate opportunities may involve specialized users who need powerful AI processing, professional graphics capabilities, or large amounts of shared memory.
Channel partners evaluating the device for customers should consider several factors:
Workload requirements: Determine whether customers need local AI processing or can continue using cloud services and existing hardware.
Software compatibility: Verify that essential applications and development tools work as expected on Nvidia’s Arm-based platform.
Total cost: Compare the laptop’s purchase price with alternatives such as conventional workstations and cloud-based AI computing.
Deployment and support: Assess security controls, device management, and ongoing support requirements before recommending enterprise adoption.
These considerations align with Dell’s broader channel strategy. The company has been expanding partner incentives focused on AI expertise and customer outcomes , creating opportunities for partners to advise customers on specialized technology deployments.
As enterprises move AI projects into production, Channel Insider has also examined how AI infrastructure challenges are creating opportunities for channel partners , particularly around helping customers evaluate the hardware, data infrastructure, and services needed to support their workloads.
The XPS 16 Creator Edition gives partners another product to evaluate as those discussions move toward purchasing decisions.
For now, the most important questions are whether customers have workloads that justify the additional hardware investment and whether the new platform can support the applications they already depend on.
For more on Dell’s expanding AI portfolio, see how the company is adding GPU acceleration and agentic AI capabilities to its enterprise data platform , creating new infrastructure and services opportunities for channel partners.

title: $5,000 Invested in Nvidia 5 Years Ago Would Be Worth $58,045 Today. Here’s How Much a $5,000 Investment Today Could Be Worth by 2031
text:
$5,000 Invested in Nvidia 5 Years Ago Would Be Worth $58,045 Today. Here’s How Much a $5,000 Investment Today Could Be Worth by 2031
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) has been one of the biggest winners of the ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. That's why the company's shares have skyrocketed over the past five years. It's worth putting some numbers behind this to understand just how impressive Nvidia's performance has been since 2021. If you had invested $5,000 in the company then and held on, that investment would be worth about $58,045 today (including dividends reinvested). Of course, what matters now is how Nvidia might perform moving forward. Let's try to determine what a $5,000 investment today might be worth by 2031.
The AI boom is still very much in full swing. We got plenty of evidence for that claim during the latest earnings season. Many major tech (or tech-adjacent) corporations continue to spend significant sums on AI infrastructure, with some even increasing their capex guidance for the fiscal year 2026.
Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is one such example. Nvidia continues to benefit from the massive AI spending. During the company's second quarter of its fiscal year 2027, for the period ended July 26, revenue soared 106% year over year to $96.2 billion. Nvidia's non-GAAP operating income came in at almost $64 billion, up 124% year over year, while its non-GAAP earnings per share jumped 120% year over year to $2.22.
These are outstanding results for a company of this size, and they sent Nvidia stock up significantly post-earnings. There could be more where that came from. According to some estimates, AI infrastructure spending will exceed $1 trillion by 2029. For context, it was about $318 billion in 2025.
Of course, projections can be wrong. But there is tangible evidence, beyond companies' spending, that the AI industry could continue to grow at a good clip. Perhaps one sign is consumer adoption of the technology. Consider that in September, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) launched what was perhaps one of the first mass-market, consumer-facing AI agents: Muse.
How did the public respond? Muse quickly rose to the top of the list of free iOS app downloads, racking up about 730,000 downloads in just five days. That at least suggests that there is a market for these kinds of products. But Meta had to spend significant sums on AI infrastructure to train advanced AI models and build AI agents on top of those models.
The lesson for other companies that want to launch consumer-facing AI agents is that it probably won't be cheap, and Nvidia's hardware, including its GPUs ( graphics processing units ) and CPUs (central processing units), can be an essential part of such a project. Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang, has predicted that there will eventually be billions of AI agents.
Perhaps that's too optimistic, but the rising prevalence of agents used within corporations and those used by individual consumers could be a powerful tailwind for the company in the medium term. Meanwhile, Nvidia still has major strengths, including a wide moat from switching costs, technological expertise, and deep relationships with many corporations, among others.
These advantages can allow the company to ride the AI tailwind over the next five years and overcome challenges such as competition.
Even though Nvidia still has massive opportunities, investors shouldn't expect the company to deliver the same returns through 2031 that it has over the past five years. But that's an incredibly high bar. The company could deliver highly competitive returns without matching its recent unreal performance.
Consider that Nvidia is currently trading at 24.9x forward earnings, compared to the 20.8x average for information technology stocks. And over the next five years, year-over-year earnings per share (EPS) growth should normalize. Assume EPS increases at an average of 15% over the next five years, and Nvidia's forward price-to-earnings drops to 22 by then.
The company would post annualized returns of roughly 12.2% over this period, turning $5,000 into about $8,885. Those are strong returns, and in my view, our assumptions are fairly defensible. Nvidia's EPS will likely grow much faster than 15% at least through the next several quarters.
All that to say: Nvidia remains in a good position to beat broader equities over the medium term. The company's shares are still a buy, despite some recent volatility.

title: Nvidia (NVDA) Deepens Its AI Infrastructure Role
text:
NVIDIA (NasdaqGS: NVDA) agreed to invest in AI lab Nous Research to support both open-weight and proprietary model development.
Microsoft introduced the Surface Laptop Ultra featuring NVIDIA's new RTX Spark processor for on-device AI workloads.
The RTX Spark chip brings NVIDIA's AI-focused graphics hardware into thinner consumer and enterprise laptops beyond data center servers.
NVIDIA's backing of Nous Research and the Surface Laptop Ultra with RTX Spark only captures part of how its AI reach is widening. Take a look at 2 warning signs (1 major) we have identified for NVIDIA.
This AI buildout touches a much wider group of hardware and chip suppliers, so it is worth scanning the broader set exposed to this theme through 92 AI infrastructure stocks .
NVIDIA, a US-based semiconductor group with a market value of about $5.6 trillion, builds data center scale AI infrastructure that underpins both training and deployment of large models. By extending that expertise into partnerships around open-weight research labs and on-device processors, the business is stretching its AI reach from hyperscale facilities into consumer and enterprise hardware.
How does backing Nous Research fit NVIDIA's broader AI strategy?
NVIDIA is putting capital behind Nous Research so that whether enterprises adopt open-weight assistants like Hermes Agent or closed models, they are more likely to run on NVIDIA hardware and software. It is a way of treating AI labs as future tenants, with NVIDIA positioned as the infrastructure landlord underneath whichever model ecosystems gain traction.
Does this Nous and RTX Spark news change the NVIDIA Narrative?
The update mainly reinforces the existing Narrative that NVIDIA is pushing full stack AI infrastructure across data centers, software and now devices, supported by strong AI CapEx and agentic AI adoption. It also touches one of the flagged risks, customer vertical integration, by trying to keep developers and labs tied into CUDA, TensorRT and NVIDIA's safety platforms rather than drifting to alternative stacks.
What should NVIDIA watchers focus on next to judge whether this matters?
The clearest near term checks are how many OEMs follow Microsoft in shipping RTX Spark based laptops and whether NVIDIA discloses concrete Nous related deployments into enterprise workflows. Updates through 2027 on agent safety platform adoption and the US$1b super intelligence commitment will also show how deeply these partnerships translate into real compute demand.

title: DLSS 5 Comes To Hogwarts Legacy & RTX Spark, Powered By 2X Faster Model
text:
DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering launched last month, enhancing lighting and materials in NBA 2K27 .
Today, we’re sharing what’s next for DLSS 5, starting with the release of the game-changing technology for NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops on October 16th.
That same day, NBA 2K27 will receive a 2X faster model that increases in-game frame rates. And the new 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model will power DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy and Where Winds Meet in the coming weeks.
Additionally, October 23rd sees the addition of DLSS 5 to RTX Remix, giving modders even more options and tools for remastering classic games.
And our team has today released a beta of a new DLSS Frame Generation Performance Mode, which you can try now by downloading the latest NVIDIA app beta update.
For further information about all of our new DLSS updates, read on.
Over the past 8 years, we’ve continuously innovated on DLSS, bringing new features, faster performance, and enhanced image quality.
This year has been our busiest yet, introducing DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation and higher Frame Generation multipliers, and delivering 2nd generation transformer AI model improvements across the entire suite of DLSS technologies.
Today, the enhancements and innovations continue.
Through a combination of systematic pipeline optimizations and neural model refinements, the performance of DLSS 5’s 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model is improving by 2X this week, enabling even more gamers to enjoy DLSS 5’s transformative uplift in lighting and materials at higher frames rates and settings.
The DLSS 5 October update shrinks the footprint by 24% to roughly 118 million parameters while reducing 4K VRAM usage by 20%. The result is half the GPU overhead of the September version while maintaining comparable visual fidelity.
DLSS 5’s 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model is now 10X faster overall compared to when it was announced in March
The new, more performant DLSS 5 model will debut in NBA 2K27 on October 16th on GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, RTX Spark laptops, and GeForce NOW, boosting frame rates by up to 1.4X. And it will ship by default with future DLSS 5 games.
NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering is coming to Hogwarts Legacy on November 5th, for GeForce RTX 50 Series, GeForce NOW, and RTX Spark.
Published by Warner Bros. Games under the Portkey Games label and developed by Avalanche Software, Hogwarts Legacy is an immersive, action, open-world role-playing-game set in the 1800s wizarding world that’s sold over 40 million copies.
Introducing an original story, the game puts fans at the center of their very own adventure. Beginning as a fifth-year student at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, players embark on a journey through new and familiar locations, discover magical beasts, craft potions, master spell casting, upgrade talents and customize their character to become the witch or wizard they want to be.
On GeForce RTX PCs and laptops, Hogwarts Legacy already includes support for DLSS Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction, accelerating and enhancing its ray-traced graphics that immerse players in the world of the famous school.
In a new update launching November 5th, DLSS Neural Rendering will be added to Hogwarts Legacy , and its other DLSS technologies upgraded to their newest versions. Avalanche Software has taken advantage of DLSS 5’s SDK controls to tune the integration to maintain the artistic intent and style of the game.
Take a look at DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy in the comparisons below.
Where Winds Meet is a Wuxia open-world action-adventure RPG developed by Everstone Studio, offering a stunning open world, engaging action-adventure gameplay, deep RPG progression, and long-term free live-service updates for players. It has more than 100 million players worldwide and has reached a peak of over 250,000 concurrent players on Steam, currently holding a Steam rating of Very Positive (with over 116,000 reviews and still climbing).
Where Winds Meet includes support for DLSS Multi Frame Generation and Super Resolution, and in the near future support for DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering will be introduced, further enhancing its world and characters. There was a ton of community demand for official support, and the developers were equally impressed with the visual upgrade to the game.
Where Winds Meet ’s DLSS 5 upgrade is coming in late November. Stay tuned to GeForce.com for updates.
Today, via a new NVIDIA app beta update , we’re introducing a new faster Performance Mode for Frame Generation, for GeForce RTX 40 Series and GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs, and RTX Spark laptops.
DLSS Multi Frame Generation and Frame Generation utilize two AI models, one that leverages game data such as motion vectors and depth to understand object motion between the two rendered frames, and a second model to calculate optical flow for elements like UI or ray-traced effects.
Labeled “Preset C,” in the NVIDIA app’s Frame Generation override, this new Performance Mode replaces the second AI model with a faster and lighter algorithm to boost frame rates for DLSS Frame Generation, Multi Frame Generation, and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, with minor trade-offs in image quality. On a GeForce RTX 5060, this Performance Mode for Frame Generation is up to 35% faster.
To apply Preset C to your games:
Download and install our newest NVIDIA app update via our website, or from inside the app itself
Open the app, and in Settings --> About, tick “Opt in to access Beta or experimental features”
Wait a moment for the beta update to download, then click the on-screen message to install
Once installed, open the “Graphics” section of the new NVIDIA app beta and select a supported Frame Generation, Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Frame Generation game (alternatively, select “Global Settings” at the top of the window and apply to every supported game in your library)
Open the “Frame Generation” drop-down and choose “Preset C” (if Preset C isn’t visible, please reboot your system)
Classic PC games are remembered for their incredible stories, characters and gameplay, but dated visuals can make them tough for modern players to enjoy. NVIDIA RTX Remix changes that. Built for RTX PCs , our modding platform uses cutting-edge path tracing, accelerated by DLSS, to reimagine timeless titles, letting longtime fans and a new generation experience era-defining games in stunning detail.
On October 23rd, we’re adding DLSS 5 with the new, faster 3D-Guided Neural Rendering model, and the faster Performance Mode for Frame Generation to RTX Remix, giving modders even more options and tools for remastering classic games.
To demonstrate the possibilities of DLSS 5 in RTX Remix, we shared a preview version with select modders, asking them to put its new capabilities to the test.
Sparkles/Kim2091 enhanced their in-development Fallout 4 RTX project with DLSS 5. In the following comparison, the soldier’s helmet has better reflections and lighting response when DLSS 5 is enabled. Additionally, his neck has better shadowing and his clothes have greater depth and material detail.
SoftSoundd enhanced their in-development Mirror’s Edge RTX project with DLSS 5. With it enabled, there are improved contact shadows and better ambient occlusion on Faith’s hand and pants, and better lighting response around the zip line, adding even more realism to the path tracing output.
To use DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering and Frame Generation with Performance Mode in RTX Remix on October 23rd, download the latest version NVIDIA RTX Remix from the Home screen of the NVIDIA app , or GitHub , press Alt + X on your keyboard to launch the NVIDIA RTX Remix Runtime User Guide overlay, and click on the Developer Settings Menu option inside the interface. Then, enable DLSS 5 in the runtime or toolkit menu as seen below.
DLSS 5 UI in the RTX Remix Toolkit
Modders have access to the same controls as developers, enabling them to include and exclude content from DLSS 5’s remit , to mask specific elements of scenes, and specify on a per object basis which DLSS 5 preset should be used and how the content should be affected. For further details, check out our DLSS 5 launch article .
DLSS accelerates performance and enhances image quality in over 1,000 games and apps, and we remain committed to further improving your experiences through the power of AI rendering.
Stay tuned to GeForce.com to learn what’s next for DLSS.
